items.followUp: Define transpiration. State how temperature, humidity, and wind affect its rate.

rubric.why: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying loss of water vapour from aerial plant parts.

rubric.why: Higher temperature and greater light intensity generally increase the rate of transpiration.
rubric.description: Explains the effects of temperature and light intensity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each factor correctly linked to an increase in the rate.

rubric.why: High humidity reduces the water-vapour gradient between the leaf and the surrounding air, lowering transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that high humidity lowers the rate.

rubric.why: Wind carries water vapour away from the leaf surface; a shortage of soil water reduces water uptake and transpiration.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of wind or soil water availability.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either a correct effect of wind or a correct effect of soil-water shortage.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.
Higher temperature generally increases the rate of transpiration.
Greater light intensity generally increases the rate of transpiration.
High humidity lowers the rate because the water-vapour gradient between the leaf and air is reduced.
Wind generally increases the rate by carrying water vapour away from the leaf surface.
A shortage of water in the soil reduces water uptake and lowers the rate of transpiration.
